name: Tojolabal
confidence_why: Furbee-Losee 1976, the only full grammar of Tojolabal and known to us only through page excerpt, gives initial word stress that moves to the last syllable when the word ends a phrase, a pattern Bennett 2016 repeats, while Lenkersdorf 2010 calls native words final-stressed and marks penultimate stress only on Spanish and Zoque loans, which matches Furbee-Losee's phrase-final layer but leaves phrase-medial initial stress resting on the 1976 analysis alone; the penultimate stress coded by StressTyp2 and Gordon 2002 is supported by neither.
catalog_quote: primary stress is assigned to the final syllable if the word is spoken in isolation, that is if it is a phrase, and still later the primary stress on the first syllable reduces to a secondary stress under the influence of the primary [stress in the following syllable] ... Primary stress is assigned to the vowel of a phrase-final syllable that ends in a consonant; thus, [..po.'wil.] derives from %…

tone.quote: A través de fluctuaciones entonacionales, los narradores tojolabales proveen al auditorio con las herramientas necesarias para interpretar de qué fuente viene la información citada y a quién le estaba dirigida originalmente. En conclusión, si bien no es posible proponer que en tojolabal haya patrones entonacionales con semántica evidencial, es factible considerar que la alteración en la frecuencia, amplitud y duración, además de en la cualidad de la voz, ayudan a marcar cambios en la fuente de información entre citas directas con distintos emisores y receptores originales o en caso de que el narrador pase de la voz narrativa al discurso citado o viceversa.
tone.locator: pp. 193-194 (the quoted passage begins with 'A' as the last word of p. 193 and continues at the top of p. 194, immediately before 'III.3 Conclusion'); section III.2.2 heading on p. 178; phrase-accent/status-suffix remark p. 116 (not 115) and p. 28
tone.translation: Through intonational fluctuations, Tojolabal narrators provide the audience with the tools needed to interpret which source the quoted information comes from and to whom it was originally addressed. In conclusion, although it is not possible to propose that Tojolabal has intonational patterns with evidential semantics, it is feasible to consider that alteration of frequency, amplitude and duration, as well as of voice quality, helps mark changes in information source between direct quotations with different original speakers and addressees, or when the narrator passes from the narrative voice to quoted speech or vice versa.
tone.summary: Pitch (F0), amplitude and duration on the phrase-accent syllable described only as discourse-level intonation used to signal quotation/source shifts; no lexical tone mentioned or claimed.

tone.quote: El tojol’ab’al es una lengua en que el acento de frase es notoriamente más prominente que el acento léxico, lo cual empata con el hecho de que el gobierno del orden lineal está regido por la estructura de la información y no por las relaciones sintácticas como en otras lenguas. En consecuencia, los hablantes no tienen acceso a una estrategia prosódica para contrastar la información focal como ocurre en inglés. Un problema semejante sucede con lenguas tonales donde no puede haber una prominencia tonal sobre un constituyente (Hartman: 1998).
tone.locator: pp. 88-89, §2.4.3 'Estrategia sintáctica: foco ex situ' (prosodic measurements pp. 32-34, §2.2.1.1, Figs. 3-5)
tone.translation: Tojol'ab'al is a language in which phrase accent is notably more prominent than lexical accent, which fits the fact that linear order is governed by information structure and not by syntactic relations as in other languages. Consequently, speakers have no access to a prosodic strategy for contrasting focal information as happens in English. A similar problem occurs with tonal languages, where there cannot be a tonal prominence on a constituent (Hartman 1998).
tone.summary: Pitch = phrase-level intonation (rising peripheries, falling predicative unit); no lexical tone claimed.
